title: Social Services Legislation Amendment (Enhanced Welfare Payment Integrity) Bill 2016
short_title: Social Services Legislation Amendment (Enhanced Welfare Payment Integrity) Bill 2016

speeches.speaker: Amanda Rishworth
speeches.brief: The bill introduces departure prohibition orders for unpaid welfare debts and removes the six-year limit on debt recovery, with a net saving of $157.8 million. Labor will not oppose it in the House but awaits a Senate committee report, while criticising the government's rhetoric on welfare recipients.

speeches.speaker: Sarah Henderson
speeches.brief: The speaker argued for the bill to allow departure prohibition orders for targeted social welfare debtors and remove the six-year limitation on debt recovery, noting that as of June 2015 there were over one million debts owed to the Commonwealth valued at $3.04 billion.

speeches.speaker: Eric Hutchinson
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Social Services Legislation Amendment (Enhanced Welfare Payment Integrity) Bill 2016 is a reasonable measure to recover overpayments from welfare recipients, citing that social services account for 35% of Commonwealth spending. They claimed Labor created a $46.9 billion budget black hole, including nearly $10 billion in social services, and blocked $13.4 billion in savings and revenue measures.

speeches.speaker: Craig Laundy
speeches.brief: The speaker argued in support of the bill to strengthen welfare debt recovery, citing $3.04 billion in outstanding debts and advocating for removing the six-year limitation on recovery and allowing travel bans for debtors, emphasising that debts are owed to Australian taxpayers.

speeches.speaker: Christian Porter
speeches.brief: The speaker argued the bill would strengthen debt recovery from former welfare recipients by allowing departure prohibition orders and removing a six-year limitation, estimating net savings of $157.8 million and targeting $870 million in debts from 270,000 former recipients.
